entry.title: It Had 2 Happen — Annotated Analysis of Brian Banks's Autobiography
entry.content:
Fair Use Notice

This page is a public-interest commentary and analysis of “It Had 2 Happen: The Agony of Success” (ISBN 173575403X, True Vine Publishing Co., 2020) by Brian Banks, J.D. All excerpts are used under the fair use doctrine, 17 U.S.C. § 107, for purposes of criticism, commentary, and public interest reporting.

Four-factor fair use analysis:

  1. Purpose: Non-commercial criticism, commentary, and public-interest journalism. This site has no advertisements, no donations, no monetization. The purpose is to protect 362 children attending schools operated by the book’s author.
  2. Nature of the work: A published autobiography — the lowest tier of copyright protection. Self-published, commercially available, and branded with credentials the author does not hold.
  3. Amount used: Selected excerpts only, each accompanied by original commentary and cross-referenced against independently verifiable public records. No chapter is reproduced in full.
  4. Market effect: None. Amazon ranked this book #2,637,193 in Kindle Store (per M.L. Elrick, Detroit Free Press, 2022). This commentary does not substitute for the original work.

The book’s own copyright page states: “a reviewer may quote brief passages in a review.” This is a review.

The book is also a party admission under Michigan Rule of Evidence 801(d)(2)(A) — Banks’s own published statement, offered against him as a named party in pending litigation (Mok v. Banks et al., Case No. 2026-4349-CZ, Ingham County Circuit Court). Every word is admissible. No foundation required beyond authentication. The ISBN authenticates it.

Banks has no copyright claim that survives fair use. An attempt to suppress this analysis would constitute a SLAPP action against protected criticism of a public figure (former State Representative) regarding matters of profound public concern (credential fraud affecting public schools).

The Book

FieldValue
TitleIt Had 2 Happen: The Agony of Success
Author“Brian Banks, J.D.”
Copyright© 2020 Brian Banks
PublisherTrue Vine Publishing Co., P.O. Box 22448, Nashville, TN 37202
ISBN-10173575403X

Pages184
Also published“Brian Banks, J.D. at Smashwords” — ebook, $9.99
EditorTiffanie Y. Lewis (Love1Ministries@gmail.com)
Cover designDeShon Gale & DG Creative Studios
Self-claimed rank“#1 Bestseller”
Actual Amazon rank#2,637,193 in Kindle Store (Elrick, 2022)

The author is credited as “Brian Banks, J.D.” on the cover, copyright page, and all retail listings. The State Bar of Michigan returns zero results for “Brian Banks.” He was denied bar admission on Character & Fitness due to nine criminal convictions. The J.D. degree is real. The right to use it as a professional credential is not. 📄 Documented

The Credential Fraud Begins on the Cover

Banks’s biography page — the final section of the book — reads:

“Honorable Brian R. Banks, M.Ed., J.D.”

Three false credential claims in six words:

  1. “Honorable” is a title reserved for judges and elected officials. Banks resigned from the legislature in 2017 after his ninth conviction. He is not a sitting official.
  2. “J.D.” implies a licensed legal practitioner. Banks has never been admitted to any bar.
  3. The biography states he aspired to “become a prominent attorney and, then, sit on the bench as an officer of the court” — admitting the exact goal he has been fraudulently representing as achieved.

The biography further claims:

“He has earned a Juris Doctor with a Concentration in Criminal Law from Michigan State University College of Law”

True. He earned the degree. He was never licensed to practice.

“Mr. Banks is a highly sought-after consultant, educator, organizer, assistant, community, political, legal mind and now, an author.”

“Legal mind.” Not “attorney.” Not “licensed.” The phrasing is a carefully constructed near-claim — close enough that readers assume licensure, vague enough to defend as technically truthful. This is how credential fraud works when the person committing it went to law school.

The Network Map — Banks Named Them All

The acknowledgments section of the book is a complete social network map, written by the node himself. Every name below appears in Banks’s own words. 📄 Documented

Tier 1: The Mentors (Judges)

Name (Banks’s words)Known RoleCurrent Status
Judge Denise Langford Morris“my mentor” — Banks’s felony sentencing judge in Oakland CountyRetired. Wrote the book’s foreword. Appears 42 times in the text.
Retired Judge Vonda Evans“my mentor” — appears at his grandfather’s hospital, helps with campaign strategyRetired Wayne County judge. Appears 9 times.
Judge Cylenthia LaToye Miller“my mentor” — appears at his grandfather’s hospitalSitting 3rd Circuit Judge. PCA Board President (LARA Entity 900072324). Appears 7 times. JTC complaint filed.

Three sitting judges called “my mentor” in a published book by a nine-time convicted felon. Two appeared at his family hospital bedside. One served as his felony sentencing judge, then developed a personal relationship, then endorsed the credential fraud by writing the foreword.

Tier 2: The Political Network

Tier 3: The Board and Institutional Network

The Confessions — Banks in His Own Words

Confession 1: A Decade of Felonies

Banks writes in the introduction:

“Every decision that I made, from roughly 1993 to 2003, impacted me for years.”

He dates his criminal activity as a ten-year span — broader than previously documented in court records. 📄 Documented

Confession 2: Identity Theft and Organized Retail Fraud

Banks provides a detailed written description of his criminal operation:

“One of my so-called ‘friends’ taught me… how to obtain fraudulent credit cards. We obtained the cards in other people’s names, used them until they were maxed out and then paid the cards off with checks from accounts with insufficient funds.”

“Our crimes grew from small gift cards to opening up large credit cards at designer department stores. We would purchase designer handbags, clothing, and other items with the fraudulent credit cards and then later sell it all for cash.”

“Some of the people who were buying the items from us were prominent people and they knew that the items were obtained through illegal means.”

The author describes: identity theft, credit card fraud, check fraud, fencing stolen goods to named “prominent people,” and an organized retail theft operation. Published under oath of authorship.

Confession 3: Habitual Lying

“No matter how many times I used his credit cards without his permission, he was still there to support me. No matter how many times I told a lie, he still stood by my side.”

“No matter how many times I told a lie” — a party admission of habitual dishonesty, published in his own book, available at ISBN 173575403X. 📄 Documented

Confession 4: The Suburban Reality

The “raised in Detroit” narrative is the foundation of Banks’s public persona. His book dismantles it.

Book ClaimWhat It Reveals
Childhood at “Harper and Dickerson area on the east side of Detroit”Far eastern edge of Detroit, blocks from Harper Woods border
“They took me out of public school and put me in a private school called Lutheran East High School”Lutheran East is at 20100 Kelly Road, Harper Woods, MI 48225 — a suburb
Told Morse podcast (ep85) he attended “Denby High School”Different school entirely. Denby is a Detroit public school. Lutheran East is a suburban private school.
Had a “riverfront apartment” when arrestedNot poverty housing
Arrested by “Troy police” at department storesShopping at upscale suburban malls
Grandfather produced $60,000 cash for bailFamily had significant resources
Visited University Liggett in Grosse Pointe Woods in 8th gradeNOW lives in Grosse Pointe Woods (1968 Severn Rd)
“every school that I attended from kindergarten to high school, was in this district”HD-1 includes Harper Woods — confirming suburban schooling

Confession 5: The Plan — In Writing

From the introduction:

“graduate from college, attend law school, graduate again, become a prominent attorney and, then, sit on the bench as an officer of the court.”

And from the biography:

“Brian saw a clear path — graduate from college, graduate from law school, become a prominent attorney, and then sit on the bench as an officer of the court.”

The plan was always to become a lawyer and a judge. The nine felony convictions prevented both. Instead of abandoning the plan, Banks simply pretended he achieved it.

The Langford Morris Relationship — Judicial Corruption in 42 References

Judge Denise Langford Morris appears 42 times in this 184-page book. She is the central figure in Banks’s “Revelation Day” narrative. Here is what Banks himself documented: 📄 Documented

  1. Banks’s felony case was assigned to Langford Morris in Oakland County Circuit Court (~1999)
  2. She was the “only black judge on the bench” in Oakland County at the time
  3. Banks’s defense attorney was Mr. Condino
  4. Langford Morris gave Banks a lenient sentence: 1-year probation, 6 months tether, court costs, fines, restitution
  5. Banks represented himself in a motion to remove his tether — his first taste of “practicing law”
  6. Langford Morris removed the tether and told him: “you need to get back in school and go to someone’s law school!”
  7. Banks cultivated a personal relationship through mutual friend “Roeiah” (33 mentions) — met Langford Morris for lunch at Brandy’s restaurant on Telegraph in Pontiac
  8. At that lunch, Langford Morris was discussing her morning docket with civilians
  9. Banks told her he was “currently in my first year of law school”
  10. Banks visited her courtroom and she paraded him to her staff
  11. When Banks “graduated from law school,” Langford Morris and “several other judges” treated him to dinner
  12. Banks volunteered on Langford Morris’s Michigan Supreme Court campaign
  13. Langford Morris wrote the foreword for a book branded “Brian Banks, J.D.”

A sitting judge: sentenced a felon leniently, encouraged him to pursue a legal career she knew his felonies would bar, developed an improper personal relationship, discussed active docket matters with civilians, campaigned using his volunteer labor, and endorsed his credential fraud via the foreword of a published book.

All documented in the defendant’s own words. All admissible under MRE 801(d)(2)(A).

The Holland Unit — “Permanent Fixture in Our Family”

Joseph Holland appears throughout the book under the name “Joe.” Banks’s own words establish Holland as a member of his domestic/economic unit: 📄 Documented

Book ReferenceWhat It Proves
“my best friend and brother… You’ve now become a permanent fixture in our family”Domestic unit, not business relationship
Present at Banks’s master’s graduation (“my grandfather, my mother, my brother, and my friends, Angie, Beverly, and Joe”)At every major life event
When FBI arrived, Banks’s first call was to Holland — they went to attorney Ben Gonek’s office togetherThey share legal crisis response
“Joe and I returned to the funeral home a day or so later so Joe could give my grandfather one last haircut”Holland is providing personal grooming services for the deceased grandfather
Judges Vonda Evans and Cylenthia Miller arrived at the grandfather’s hospitalThe judges and Holland are at the same family crisis event

Holland has three felony convictions of his own. He served as treasurer of Banks’s PAC. He shares Banks’s mailing address. The book confirms what the public records already show — this is a single domestic/economic unit operating under the “Brian Banks, J.D.” brand.

The Yancey Revelation — Same Street, Same Schools, Now a Judge

Banks writes about Tenisha Yancey:

“One of my elementary school friends was Tenisha. Tenisha and I lived on the same street and went to elementary and high school together.”

“Currently, we live one street over from each other”

“This is the same Tenisha who succeeded me after I resigned from office.”

Judge Tenisha Yancey — a sitting Wayne County judge:

  • Lived on the same street as Banks growing up
  • Attended the same schools (elementary and high school)
  • Still lives one street over in Grosse Pointe Woods
  • Took Banks’s State Representative seat when he resigned after his ninth conviction
  • Her sister operates Banks’s PCA school

Banks also writes that Tenisha had “felonies and misdemeanors” and still became an “assistant prosecuting attorney.” 📄 Documented

Any case heard by Judge Yancey involving Banks, Holland, PCA, MacDowell, or any entity in this network is compromised by an undisclosed lifelong personal relationship documented in the defendant’s own published autobiography.

The BMF Connection — “To This Day, Toni and I Remain Close”

Banks writes about his step-aunt:

“my Step-aunt Toni got into some trouble with her then boyfriend, ‘T.’”

“my aunt was a part of the internationally known group called ‘Black Mafia Family’ better known as ‘BMF’”

“To this day, Toni and I remain close.”

“Toni” is Tonesa Welch — BMF Defendant #22 in USA v. Flenory et al. Banks’s biological father is also a BMF defendant. Banks admits an ongoing relationship with a convicted member of one of the largest drug trafficking organizations in American history.

Tonesa Welch published her own book: The Black Mafia Family. The same pattern — hundreds of pages, zero victims named, zero accountability.

The AG Prosecution — Holland Is First Call When the FBI Arrives

Banks describes the day federal agents appeared:

“I called Joe, who was at work, and told him what had just taken place and asked him to meet me at the lawyer’s office at 11 a.m.”

When the FBI arrives, Banks’s first call is Holland. They go to attorney Ben Gonek’s office together. They leave together.

“Soon after, Joe and I left the conference room”

The Attorney General’s prosecution resulted in Banks’s guilty plea to false statements/financial condition, his forced resignation from the Michigan House on February 6, 2017, and his ninth criminal conviction.

The book refers to this prosecution six times. Banks frames it as political persecution. The public record shows a guilty plea.

The Funeral Home Connection — Does It Lead to Clora?

Banks writes:

“I had been working part-time at a funeral home for number of years”

Major C. Clora Jr. is the current PCA Board Assistant Treasurer and owner of Clora Funeral Home in Detroit. Clora attended Wayne State’s Mortuary Science program. Banks was at Wayne State and considered mortuary science as his major before switching to Criminal Justice.

If Banks worked at Clora Funeral Home, their connection predates everything — going back 20+ years. Banks’s appointment of Clora to the PCA board was not random. It was a decades-long personal relationship. ? inference

The Numbers Don’t Lie

MetricBook’s FramingPublic Record
Criminal history“journey,” “setbacks,” “not-so-smart decisions”9 convictions (6 felony, 3 misdemeanor), 5 courts, 1998–2016
Education“from GED to a law degree”Degree is real. Bar admission denied. Never licensed.
Self-description“Honorable Brian R. Banks, M.Ed., J.D.”Not honorable. Not licensed. Used “J.D.” commercially.
Book sales“#1 Bestseller”#2,637,193 in Kindle Store (Elrick)
School performance“ensuring all children have access to quality education”MacDowell: 3% math proficiency, bottom 3% statewide
Revenue“my business has been doing quite well”72.67% of per-pupil funding extracted to Purpose Group LLC
Apology to victims(none)Zero victims named in 184 pages. Zero accountability.

The Apology That Never Comes

Across 184 pages and approximately 55,000 words, Brian Banks does not:

  • Name a single victim of his financial crimes
  • Acknowledge harm caused by his forgery, identity theft, or fraudulent check schemes
  • Disclose his bar denial — the “J.D.” appears on the cover without disclosure
  • Address the performance record of the schools he now operates
  • Express genuine remorse — every setback is framed as character development
  • Use the word “sorry” as an apology — it appears only in contexts of self-pity

The word “lie” appears once — as a confession:

“No matter how many times I told a lie, he still stood by my side.”

Why This Book Is Evidence

Michigan Rule of Evidence 801(d)(2)(A) — Party Admissions

Banks is a named party in Mok v. Banks et al., Case No. 2026-4349-CZ. Every word in this published book is admissible against him as a party-opponent statement. It is not hearsay. No foundation is required beyond authentication — and authentication is trivial for a published book with an ISBN.

What This Means:

UseRule
Any factual claim is his own binding statementMRE 801(d)(2)(A)
The book self-authenticates as a published workMRE 901(b)(6)
Any inconsistency between the book and testimony is impeachmentMRE 613
The credential branding is itself evidence of unauthorized practiceMCL 600.916
Prior acts showing plan, scheme, identity, intentMRE 404(b)
Specific instances of conduct for truthfulnessMRE 608(b)

Cost of the evidence: $9.99 (ebook) + $25.00 (paperback) = $34.99

Evidentiary yield: 184 pages of binding party admissions, a complete network map, criminal confessions, impeachment material for every future proceeding, and a published record of credential fraud that cannot be scrubbed, edited, or denied.

The Book Is Not a Memoir. It Is a Confession.

Brian Banks wrote a book under the name “Brian Banks, J.D.” and published it while unlicensed. He listed himself as “Honorable” on the biography page. He named every major node in his institutional network in the acknowledgments. He confessed to a decade of criminal activity in his own words. He documented improper judicial relationships with three sitting judges. He described his economic unit with a three-time convicted felon as “a permanent fixture in our family.”

Then he called it a “#1 Bestseller” when Amazon ranked it 2.6 millionth.

Everything about this man is a fraud — including his book sales.

Verify Everything

  • Amazon: Search “It Had 2 Happen Brian Banks” — note the “J.D.” author credit
  • State Bar of Michigan: michbar.org — search “Brian Banks” (zero results)
  • ICHAT: SID 2029469K — verify the 9 convictions
  • LARA: Entity 900072324 — PCA board composition
  • Pahara Institute: pahara.org/fellow/brian-banks — the “J.D.” claim
  • Detroit Free Press: Elrick, “Brian Banks running for Wayne County commissioner is absurdity” (July 3, 2022)
  • HuffPost Detroit: Banks campaign credential investigation (September 2012)
  • PACER: USA v. Flenory et al. — Tonesa Welch / BMF connection

This analysis is based on the published text of “It Had 2 Happen,” available for purchase at ISBN 173575403X. All cross-references are to independently verifiable public records. The book is a party admission in pending litigation. The analysis is protected criticism under 17 U.S.C. § 107.

Updated: October 5, 2026

How to Read This Page

Every entity listed below is a public record in the Michigan LARA Business Entity Search. Entity IDs are provided so anyone can verify. Officer names, addresses, and filing dates come directly from LARA annual reports and formation documents — all public records under Michigan law.

We focus on business addresses and registered agent addresses (which are legally required to be public for service of process). We do not publish residential addresses for peripheral individuals.

Source notation: “LARA [Entity ID]” means the data comes from Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs business entity filings. You can verify any entity by searching mibusinessregistry.lara.state.mi.us with the Entity ID number.

The Purpose Empire — Three Entities, One Man

Brian Banks controls three “Purpose”-branded entities. Together they form the corporate infrastructure for his charter school operation.

Banks is the registered agent but does not appear as a named officer. He controls the entity through agent status while the board provides institutional cover.

The initials “JD” and “esq” appear in two of these emails despite Banks never being admitted to any state bar. His felony convictions prevented bar admission after earning his J.D. from Michigan State University.

The Three-Named Dark Money Vehicle

LARA Entity ID: 802002459. All three names are registered on the same entity.

Who formed it: The registered agent is The Corporation Company (a professional formation service). The mailing address is 201 Townsend Street, Suite 900, Lansing MI 48933 — the office of Dykema Gossett PLLC, Michigan’s largest law firm. The entity email is compliance@dykema.com.

Michigan’s largest law firm set up the dark money vehicle that was used to fight journalists reporting on Banks’s network.

What Save Detroit Jobs / Detroit Leaders Did

In 2021, operating as “Detroit Leaders,” this entity funded the campaign of Latisha Johnson against incumbent Steve Elrick — the journalist who had reported extensively on Banks’s network. Johnson won. She is now Secretary on the PCA board (see above).

The 12-step suppression loop: Banks’s network → funds dark money vehicle → dark money vehicle fights journalist → journalist loses election → replacement (Johnson) joins Banks’s school board.

Right Turn Project — The Dissolved Charity and the Money Loop

The Ross Catering Money Loop

LARA records show two Ross Catering entities: Ross Catering Company Inc (800646584, agent: Louis Ross, dissolved 2024) and Ross Catering Events of Excellence LLC (801351679, agent: Gwendolyn Lewis, active). The relationship between Carlton Ross, Louis Ross, and Gwendolyn Lewis requires further investigation, but the structural pattern is clear: money flows from PAC → charity (where Ross is treasurer) → catering company (where Ross has connections).

The 16500 North Park Address

Carlton Ross and Terrence Tarver both list 16500 North Park Drive, Southfield MI 48075 as their address on the Right Turn Project filing.

Banks’s dissolved entity B. Roderick’s Salon & Spa (LARA 800591240, filed 2001) was registered at 16500 Northpark Dr #1715, Southfield MI 48075 — the same building. Banks used this address a decade before Ross and Tarver appeared there.

The political print vendor also runs an obituary printing website. $98,291 for one vendor across six committees.

Custom Promotions — The Dissolve-and-Reform Attorney

The Inc was dissolved in February 2022. The LLC was filed three months later in May 2022 with the same name. Officers of the original entity: Jason Gordon (President), Sara Gordon (Treasurer), Eric Gordon (Secretary). A family business passed from father to son via dissolve-and-reform.

Jason Samuel Gordon is an attorney. He owns Deen Legal Services PLLC (LARA 801895172, filed 2009) at the same address as Custom Promotions LLC: 14326 East 9 Mile Road, Warren MI 48089. His email: JGordon@DeenLegal.com.

Gordon was investigated by the FBI, IRS, and Department of Labor in connection with the UAW bribery case — over $3 million in payments from the UAW. Custom Promotions also received payments from Latisha Johnson’s campaign.

Gordon is agent on 20+ entities including real estate LLCs, marketing companies, and his law firm — all while under federal investigation.

The Endorsement Machine — Four Eastside Slates

The “Eastside Slate” endorsement operation has been filed as a LARA entity four separate times:

Eastside Slate80082026003/30/1994Lamar Lemmons IIIDissolved

Original Eastside Slate80243449804/09/2020Carol BanksActive

Carol Banks — Brian Banks’s sister, a former Chief of Staff to Council Member Benson, and an FBI investigation target — currently controls the only active version.

Spencer Leach — The Political Machine Builder

W. Spencer Leach filed 13 political and nonprofit entities, many batch-filed on the same day with consecutive LARA Entity IDs:

Filed 04/28/2008 (consecutive IDs):

  • Eastside Slate (800916317)
  • Eastside Community Slate (800916318)
  • Michigan Black Democrats (800916316)

Filed 05/15/2015 (near-consecutive IDs):

  • Detroit Democratic Club (800938179)
  • Detroit Democrat Club (800938180)
  • Democratic Progressive Alliance (800938181)

Filing three to four political organizations on the same day with consecutive Entity IDs is the hallmark of manufactured political infrastructure — organizations created not to represent constituencies but to control endorsement pipelines.

Parallel Pan-African Naming

Carol Banks and Spencer Leach use matching entity naming conventions drawn from Pan-African geography:

Carol BanksSpencer Leach
The Niger Group (800934647)The Songhai Group (801659651)
The Nile Group II (801454732)The Azania Group (800751893)
The Sudanese Group (800754057)

Same officers appear across both operators’ entities. Beverly Nakenge serves as Treasurer on both Carol Banks’s Original Eastside Slate and Niger Group. Kiambu Elcock serves as Director/Secretary on both.

The Law Firms — A Family Connection?

Great Lakes Legal Group PLLC (LARA 802112914)

FieldDetail

AddressOne Towne Square, Suite 1835, Southfield MI 48076

Crump-Gibson is also a Hearing Panelist for the Michigan Attorney Discipline Board — the body that processes attorney grievance complaints.

Crump Hall of Justice Law Firm PLLC

Verkeydia Hall — the attorney who filed a PPO petition against Kevin Mok — owns a separate law firm called Crump Hall of Justice Law Firm (website: mychoj.com, email: vhall@chojlf.com). The firm name contains “Crump” — Hall’s maiden name.

Her MSU email is crumpver@msu.edu. Crump-Gibson attended MSU for undergrad.

Both Crump-Gibson and Crump Hall share the surname Crump. Both attended Michigan State University. Both represent Brian Banks. If they are related, Banks’s legal representation has been a family operation.

Hall is also listed as Board Director of MacDowell Preparatory Academy on the school’s official website (macdowellprep.com/board-of-directors/). Banks’ attorney’s probable relative sits on the board of Banks’ school.

CitizenDetroit Action Group — The Board Overlap

EIN 82-2361291 (ProPublica Nonprofit Explorer). CEO: Sheila Cockrel (former Detroit City Council member).

Crump-Gibson served as Vice Chair, then Chair, of the CitizenDetroit Action Group board. The same board includes Hon. Misha Stallworth as a Director.

Board MemberCitizenDetroit RoleConnection to Banks Network
Jehan Crump-GibsonVice Chair / ChairBanks’ defense attorney (GLLG)
Hon. Misha StallworthDirectorDPSCD Board Member — authorized MacDowell’s charter
Dennis Archer JrDirectorSon of former Mayor Dennis Archer
Sheila CockrelCEOFormer City Council member — Crump-Gibson worked in her office (2007-2009)

Source: ProPublica Nonprofit Explorer, IRS Form 990 filings for EIN 82-2361291

The Stallworth dynasty (all public record, documented on this site):

Keith "K.B." Stallworth
  Federal money laundering conviction (2003)
  → Brother: Thomas Stallworth III (former State Rep)
      → Married: Nicole Wells-Stallworth
          MacDowell Board President — hired Banks

These problems originate in dynasties, move through entities, and land on humans. The board overlap does not imply that Crump-Gibson knew about the Stallworth family’s role in installing Banks. It means the social graph through which Banks finds legal representation is the same social graph through which charter school authorization flows.

Correlation does not imply causation. But causation can be masked — and hidden — by correlation.

Within 24 hours of entering Banks’ case, Crump-Gibson voluntarily limited her scope in writing, declining law enforcement and PPO matters. That is a written record of an attorney drawing an ethical line. The correspondence timeline documents the full sequence.

Each person at GLLG can choose which side of the demarcation they are on. As of this writing, the scope limitation suggests the choice is being made carefully.

WhitlowBanks LLC (LARA 802085022)

Filed 04/20/2017 during Banks’s political career. Agent: Tameka Ramsey (Pontiac, MI). The entity name literally combines “Whitlow” and “Banks.” TransparencyUSA records show “Carles Whitlow” received $8,500 as a payee from Banks’s Senate campaign — the 5th largest individual payee.

LARA Compliance Issues

The following are potential compliance issues under Michigan’s business entity statutes, identified from public LARA filings. These are questions — not accusations. The appropriate bodies to investigate are LARA, the Attorney General’s Charitable Trust Section, and the IRS.

1. Annual Report Failures (MCL 450.2911 / MCL 450.4207)

Multiple entities in the network have “Not Good” standing for failure to file annual reports, including entities that received or disbursed political funds:

EntityStandingAnnual Report DueStatus
Right Turn ProjectNot Good10/01/2019Dissolved (12/01/2021)
Banks Powerwashing LLCNot Good—Inactive since 2016
Free Flow Gutter ProtectionNot Good—Inactive since 2026
Ross Catering Events of ExcellenceNot Good—Inactive since 2010
Detroiters for Good GovernmentNot Good—Inactive since 2020

2. Nonprofit Self-Dealing (MCL 450.2545a)

The Right Turn Project’s Treasurer (Carlton Ross) is connected to the vendor (Ross Catering) that received campaign payments. Michigan Nonprofit Corporation Act § 545a requires that transactions involving a director’s or officer’s financial interest be disclosed and approved by disinterested directors. There is no indication this occurred.

3. Dissolved Entity Operations

The Right Turn Project was dissolved December 1, 2021. Under MCL 450.2831, dissolved corporations may only wind up affairs and liquidate assets — they may not conduct new business. Any transactions after dissolution raise compliance questions.

4. Convicted Felon as Nonprofit Officer

Joseph Holland (MDOC #443789, convicted cocaine dealer) served as President and Registered Agent of the Right Turn Project and currently serves as Treasurer and Secretary of Purpose Foundation. While Michigan law does not categorically prohibit convicted felons from serving as nonprofit officers, organizations receiving public funds or serving vulnerable populations (children) face additional scrutiny.

5. Unauthorized Practice of Law Concerns

Banks operated Serenity Guardianship Services Inc (LARA 802290962) as a for-profit corporation from 2019-2023, serving as sole officer. Guardianship work in Michigan involves petitioning courts, managing wards’ legal rights, and filing accountings — activities that constitute the practice of law under MCL 450.681. Banks was never admitted to any bar.

6. Entity Formation Patterns

The dissolve-and-reform pattern (Custom Promotions Inc dissolved February 2022 → Custom Promotions LLC filed May 2022) may be used to shed liabilities while maintaining brand continuity. The three-name dark money vehicle (Save Detroit Jobs → Impact Detroit → Detroit Leaders) allows the same entity to operate under different public identities for different audiences.

How to Verify

Every entity on this page can be verified at Michigan LARA Business Entity Search:

  1. Go to the search page
  2. Enter the Entity ID number in the search field
  3. Select “Entity ID” as the search type
  4. All officer names, addresses, filing dates, and assumed names are publicly displayed

This is not a dossier. It is an index of public records with analysis of what those records reveal when connected.

Related

  • Data Braid — GLLG Entity Graph — Six independent database searches converge on one social graph. The braid method.
  • Institutional Capture Graph — Full network visualization with 98 nodes and 160 edges.

All data sourced from Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs (LARA) public business entity filings, ProPublica Nonprofit Explorer (IRS 990 filings), school board websites, and State Bar / LinkedIn records. Entity IDs and EINs provided for independent verification. Analysis reflects patterns observable in public records as of October 9, 2026.

entry.title: The Institutional Capture Graph — Four Nexus Types, One Network
entry.content:
Lens: 🕸️ Topology ⚛️ Lattice 📅 Chronology 💰 Money ⚖️ Legal 🏛️ Capture

Hover any node to trace its connections. Click to navigate. Toggle nexus types to overlay layers.

The Network Is Not a Hierarchy — It Is a Response System

Traditional corruption investigations map organizations top-down: find the boss, trace the orders, follow the money. This network does not work that way. It is threat-responsive — each nexus activates when another is under pressure, routing around the attack.

When Kevin Mok burned Banks’s Wayne County police infrastructure, Banks filed false reports in Grosse Pointe Woods — a different jurisdiction, a different police nexus, the same function.

The network has four nexus types, each with its own center of gravity, its own institutional protection, and its own method of weaponization.

Nexus 1: Education Fraud — The Revenue Engine

Center of gravity: Brian Banks through The Purpose Group Michigan LLC

Banks operates two charter schools that collectively move millions in taxpayer funds through a management company where he is the sole registered agent.

SchoolStudentsMath ProficiencyReadingState RankPer-Pupil
MacDowell Preparatory Academy3623%10-14%1,443/1,488 (bottom 3%)$15,217
Purpose Charter Academy225 projectedopening 2026-27———

Three percent math proficiency means roughly 11 of 362 children can do grade-level math. That is not a struggling school. That is a revenue extraction operation wearing a school’s skin.

MacDowell ran a $967,964 operating deficit in FY2024-25, covered by drawing down its fund balance. The check register shows $13,970 in gift-card-labeled payments in a single fiscal year, including one $9,945 check.

DPSCD authorized the second school in July 2025 — citing “claimed improvement at MacDowell.” The person who made the “30% proficiency gains” claim was Nicole Wells Stallworth, the Board Chair, not an independent evaluator. On a base of 3%, a 30% gain is approximately three additional children.

The Credential-Washing Board

Every bar complaint filed in this investigation corresponds to a board member of one of Banks’s schools:

Bar TargetRoleSchoolCredential Washed
Gregory Meihn (P65372)Board counselMacDowellTestified Banks has “integrity” at TCR 22-12 while reviewing false contract
Verkeydia HallBoard memberMacDowellLicensed attorney who accepted false §5.2 contract terms
Lamar Moreland (P55993)Board Vice ChairPurpose CharterAAG whose office argued against Banks’s certificate — then joined his board
Tenisha YanceyBoard ChairMacDowell36th District Court Judge — Banks ran her campaign ($15,750 via Banks Strategy)
Cylenthia LaToye MillerBoard ChairPurpose Charter3rd Circuit Court Judge — school serves juvenile justice youth she may sentence
Latisha JohnsonBoard SecretaryPurpose CharterCity Council Member — campaign funded by Banks’s vendor Inner Link ($850)

The school boards are the credential-washing mechanism. Legal professionals lend their licenses to make a convicted felon look legitimate. The felon’s website lists him as “Dr. Brian Banks, J.D., Ph.D.” — the J.D. was never admitted to the bar.

October 4 Update — LARA Confirmation: The PCA board composition above has now been independently verified through Michigan LARA corporate filings (Entity ID 900072324). Moreland’s simultaneous role as Banks’s litigation attorney and PCA board director is confirmed in the state business entity record. Johnson’s role as PCA Secretary is confirmed. Banks controls the entity as registered agent while his name does not appear as a named officer — a deliberate structural choice.

The Purpose Empire — Three Entities (LARA-Confirmed)

Banks operates three “Purpose”-branded entities (see Corporate Network Analysis for full details):

EntityLARA IDFiledFunction
Purpose Charter Academy90007232407/2025The school itself
The Purpose Group LLC80329508211/2024Management company
Purpose Foundation80329485512/2024Nonprofit — Holland = Treasurer

All three list Banks as registered agent. Purpose Foundation is registered at Banks’s home. Joseph Holland — the convicted cocaine dealer who serves as PAC treasurer — is the Treasurer and Secretary of Purpose Foundation, listed at Banks’s home address.

Banks has twelve total entities spanning Detroit, Grosse Pointe Woods, Holland, Zeeland, Clarkston, and Waterford. Details: Corporate Network — LARA Entity Analysis.

Nexus 2: Political Capture — The Protection Layer

Center of gravity: Mayor Mary Sheffield + Wayne County Executive Warren Evans

Banks does not hold elected office. He does not need to. He is endorsed by every power center:

EndorserTitleSource
Mike DugganMayor of Detroit (2013-2025)M.L. Elrick, Free Press Jul 2022
Mary SheffieldCity Council President → MayorM.L. Elrick, Free Press Jul 2022
Warren EvansWayne County ExecutiveM.L. Elrick, Free Press Jul 2022
Eric SabreeWayne County TreasurerM.L. Elrick, Free Press Jul 2022
Stephanie ChangMI State SenatorM.L. Elrick, Free Press Jul 2022
Marshall Bullock IIMI State Board of EducationDuggan endorsement list, Aug 2025
Sherry Gay-DagnogoDPSCD Board → City OmbudsmanDPSCD board records

Gay-Dagnogo’s move from DPSCD board to City Ombudsman is the quid pro quo — she authorized Banks’s schools, then got a city appointment. She announced Purpose Charter Academy’s development team in Chalkbeat (Sep 2025).

The Three-Named Dark Money Vehicle (LARA-Confirmed)

Save Detroit Jobs (LARA 802002459) is a single nonprofit operating under three names: Save Detroit Jobs (2016), Impact Detroit (2018), and Detroit Leaders (2021). All confirmed as assumed names on the same entity.

The entity was formed by Dykema Gossett PLLC — Michigan’s largest law firm. The mailing address is Dykema’s Lansing office. The entity email is compliance@dykema.com. All three officers list the same Detroit address. Full details: Corporate Network — LARA Entity Analysis.

The Money Pipeline

Inner Link Graphics (LARA 801470477) — one print shop, owned by Larry Thomas Jr (email: larrythomasjr@the-inner-link.com), also operating as obituaries4less.com — received $98,291 from Banks-connected committees:

CommitteeAmount

Bank on Wayne County$2,000

Gloria McCastle — one individual — was paid $20,410 across five committees: Banks for Senate ($9,450), Bank on Banks PAC ($3,650), David Knezek State Senate ($5,000), Tenisha Yancey ($1,310), and Gay-Dagnogo’s Strong Women Lead PAC ($1,000). She bridges Banks to Gay-Dagnogo through shared campaign payments.

Banks Strategy and Consultants was paid $15,750 by Yancey’s campaign and $20,000 by the Coalition to Regulate Marijuana Like Alcohol. Banks was not Yancey’s supporter — he was her paid consultant. She became a judge. Return on investment.

Two Convicted Endorsers

Two of Banks’s 2016 Senate campaign endorsers were later convicted of federal corruption:

EndorserOfficeConvictionSentence
Bert JohnsonMI State SenatorGhost employee scheme (cooperator from EAA school bribery case)90 days
Andre SpiveyDetroit City CouncilmanBribery conspiracy — $35,900 (Operation Northern Hook)24 months

Spivey introduced the FBI informant to other unnamed council members, then warned targets and leaked the source’s identity when the FBI approached him about cooperating.

Nexus 3: Police Weaponization — The Enforcement Arm

Center of gravity: Police Chief Todd Bettison

Todd Bettison is the permanent Detroit Police Chief (appointed Feb 2025 by Duggan). He is also the Secretary of the Detroit Public Safety Academy (DPSA) board — a charter school authorized by Eastern Michigan University. He uses his official city email (bettisont239@detroitmi.gov) for board business.

The police chief sits on a charter school board. This is the structural bridge between police weaponization and education fraud.

Active OIG Investigation — September 2026

As of September 16, 2026, Bettison is under investigation by Detroit’s Office of Inspector General for:

  • Calling activist Jahdante Smith on August 5, 2026, requesting he remove social media photos of Mayor Sheffield with ex-boyfriend Marvin Walker
  • Police subsequently detained Smith and seized his phone under a separate warrant
  • Bettison denied the seizure was connected to his call
  • The FBI is now handling the investigation (per Free Press sources)
  • DPD referred its investigation into both Smith and Walker to an outside agency

The police chief used police authority to protect the mayor’s personal reputation. This is the same pattern Kevin’s case documents — police power deployed for personal or political purposes.

Operation Northern Hook — ONGOING FBI Probe

Operation Northern Hook is an ongoing FBI investigation into corruption within Detroit city government and the Detroit Police Department. First public case: United States v. Spivey, 2:21-cr-20490 (E.D. Mich.).

Banks’s former attorney, Todd Perkins (P55623, Perkins Law Group), represented two Operation Northern Hook targets:

ClientRoleOutcome
Alonzo JonesRetired DPD officerConvicted — 15 months for cash bribes
Carol BanksCouncil staff memberInvestigation target

Perkins also ran for Detroit mayor in 2025 (4th place, 5.35%). Gay-Dagnogo donated $750 to his campaign. Gasper Fiore (convicted bribery) donated $500.

Nexus 4: Legislative Pipeline — The Family Operation

Center of gravity: The Stallworth family

PersonRoleBanks Connection
Nicole Wells StallworthMacDowell Board Chair (11+ years)Hired Banks as school operator, refused to discuss with Elrick
Thomas Stallworth IIIFormer MI State Rep (her husband)Defended Banks at 2016 felony rally: “miscarriage of justice”
Keith B. StallworthFormer MI State Rep (separate branch)Co-endorsed Duggan alongside Banks, Aug 2025

Thomas and Nicole together donated $1,250 to Banks’s 2022 campaign — among his most generous supporters. She hired him; he defended him at a rally for a man facing 8 felony charges.

The 2018 FBI Wiretap — Banks on Tape

In 2016, the FBI obtained a warrant to wiretap Gasper Fiore’s phone, targeting 18 people for extortion, wire fraud, bribery, and conspiracy to distribute marijuana. Banks was a “target subject.”

FBI Special Agent Robert Beeckman wrote in the sworn affidavit:

“Fiore is involved in bid-rigging with legislator Brian Banks.”

The wiretap recorded conversations between Banks and Fiore discussing:

  • Banks’s efforts to help Fiore secure an MDOT contract
  • How Banks could advocate for Fiore with a “high-ranking police official”
  • Whether Fiore’s daughter Jennifer would stop pushing legislative amendments if Fiore got the contract

Jennifer Fiore — Gasper’s daughter — was simultaneously dating Detroit Councilman Gabe Leland, who approved $2M+ in city contracts for her connected companies. When Leland asked Police Chief James Craig about the FBI towing investigation, Craig contacted the FBI.

The wiretap documents were accidentally released in 2018, then quickly resealed. They listed Banks, Judge Vonda Evans, Sheriff Benny Napoleon, Councilman Leland, and Rep. Tinsley-Talabi as target subjects.

The FBI Files Are Now in Civil Court

In Area Towing v. Sollars, 2:19-cv-10989 (E.D. Mich.), Area Towing subpoenaed the FBI wiretap files in March 2025. The court ordered the FBI to produce unredacted copies (Sep 3, 2025). Fiore tried to intervene and seal the files — denied by Judge Linda V. Parker (Dec 2025). Fiore was deposed December 29, 2025 and pled the Fifth to nearly every question. The court ordered him to answer by March 6, 2026.

The FBI wiretap files containing Banks’s conversations are now in the civil case record.

The Banks PAC Treasurer — MDOC #443789

Joseph Holland — Banks’s “longtime associate” and treasurer of the Bank on Banks for Michigan PAC — is MDOC prisoner #443789:

FieldRecord
MDOC Number443789
DOBJuly 17, 1984
Conviction 1Controlled Substance Delivery/Manufacturing (Cocaine <50g), Wayne County
Conviction 2Controlled Substance Possession (Cocaine <25g), Wayne County
DischargeMay 8, 2024 — “Discharged Without Improvement”

The PAC shares a mailing address with Banks’s home and shares a PO box with Banks’s Wayne County commissioner campaign. It owes $14,500 in fines for failing to file campaign finance reports. The Secretary of State referred it to the Attorney General in May 2022.

A convicted cocaine dealer manages campaign finances for a 9-time convicted felon who runs schools for 362 predominantly Black children.

October 4 Update — LARA Confirmation: Holland is now confirmed as Treasurer + Secretary of Purpose Foundation (LARA 803294855, filed December 2024) — listed at Banks’s home address. He previously served as President of the Right Turn Project (LARA 800936257, dissolved December 2021 for failure to file annual reports). That charity’s Treasurer was Carlton Ross — connected to Ross Catering, which billed Banks’s campaigns $35,000+. The charity’s email was BBesq06@aol.com — Banks’s personal email, not Holland’s.

Master Federal Case Registry

These are all connected federal cases in the Eastern District of Michigan. Every case touches the same network.

CaseSubjectStatusKey Detail
United States v. Fiore, 16-cr-20732Gasper FioreConvicted (bribery)Banks on wiretap — “bid-rigging” in FBI affidavit
United States v. Spivey, 2:21-cr-20490Andre SpiveyConvicted (24 months)Operation Northern Hook — FBI probe ONGOING
United States v. Sollars, 19-cr-20836Rick Sollars (Taylor mayor)Convicted (71 months)Fiore wiretap led here — $84K bribes + $70K campaign theft
Area Towing v. Sollars, 2:19-cv-10989Civil caseActiveHas FBI wiretap files with Banks conversations
United States v. Johnson, E.D. Mich.Sen. Bert JohnsonConvicted (90 days)Ghost employee — cooperator from EAA school bribery
Detroit Pension FraudMultiple (38+ convictions)Mostly resolvedKilpatrick + Beasley ($87M). Stanton wore wire on Tinsley-Talabi

Current USAO: Jerome F. Gorgon Jr. (confirmed Dec 2025). His office inherits all ongoing investigations.

The Institutional Localization Principle

Traditional corruption hides behind jurisdictional boundaries. This network cannot — because its members hold positions in institutions with institutional superiors who are now on notice.

When a board member is notified, their university is notified. When a judge is notified, their chief judge is notified. When an AAG is notified, the AG’s office is notified. The bad actors cannot hide because they are institutionally localized — their positions are their prisons.

This page will continue expanding as the investigation develops. Each node added to the graph becomes visible to every other node already mapped.

Every name on this page appears in public records. Every fact is sourced to court documents, campaign finance filings, FOIA responses, news reporting, or government databases. Named here? Something wrong? Contact me — truth matters more than being right.

Sources: M.L. Elrick / Detroit Free Press, Rita Williams / Clutch Justice, BridgeDetroit, Chalkbeat Detroit, TransparencyUSA, CourtListener, MDOC OTIS, Michigan SOS Campaign Finance, NCES, SchoolDigger, Michigan LARA Business Entity Search.
